clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-360 at block 62,840,912: DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE to a B20 token, the B20 factory and the Policy Registry from a frame whose msg.sender is the PoolManager, as a hook or unlock callback would make (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/PoolManager.sol:104-110, src/types/Currency.sol:48).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran the read-only eth_call set of scripts/l360.py against https://mainnet.base.org at block 62,868,244 on reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/base/v1.5.6. DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE to OUSD 0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344, the factory 0xB20f000000000000000000000000000000000000 and the registry 0x8453000000000000000000000000000000000002 from a helper called by the PoolManager all return success 0 with 0x0d89438e. A plain CALL of transfer fails with 0xdb42144d naming the helper 0xc0ffee01 as the account, so the token debits the direct caller. eth_getCode of the token returns 0xef, so it is a precompile with a placeholder byte. balanceOf(PoolManager) now reads 0x5835ad5dcc7. I fetched crates/common/precompiles/src/macros.rs at base v1.5.6 and v1.6.0-rc.9: the two files are identical and line 13 returns DelegateCallNotAllowed when input.is_direct_call() is false. In src/ the PoolManager reaches outside code only by CALL: Hooks.sol:134 uses call, Currency.sol:48 and the ERC20 branch use call, and PoolManager.sol:110 calls unlockCallback on msg.sender. src/ has no DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE (grep over src/ finds only the NoDelegateCall modifier and test mocks). A contract called this way is itself the direct caller of the token, so it cannot spend the PoolManager's balance.

clearedSpotChecks.check: New Base tags v1.6.0-rc.8 and rc.9: interpreter, integer library and precompile wrapper.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched Cargo.lock at base/base v1.6.0-rc.9 and at v1.5.6 from raw.githubusercontent.com. Apart from checksum lines, rc.9 matches the copy the researcher saved. It pins revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, revm-precompile 43.0.3 and ruint 1.19.0, and the saved rc.8 lockfile has the same interpreter and ruint versions. The running build v1.5.6 pins revm 42.0.1, revm-interpreter 42.0.0 and ruint 1.19.0, so the running integer library is not at 1.21.0. The rc.9 interpreter is a different version from the running build, so it is reassuring only for a future release. The interpreter that runs today is covered by the battery and pmdiff results. I did not fetch the rc.7 lockfile, so the claim that rc.9 equals rc.7 rests on the saved rc.8 copy.
